name: Game leaderboard

input.query: WITH page AS ( SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY r.conservative DESC, m.id) AS rank,        m.id::text AS model_id, u.handle AS owner, m.version,        m.weight_class::text AS class, m.size_bytes,        r.conservative AS rating, (r.matches_played < 20) AS provisional,        r.matches_played AS matches FROM models m JOIN users u ON u.id = m.owner_id JOIN games g ON g.id = m.game_id JOIN ratings r ON r.model_id = m.id AND r.ladder = ($2)::ladder WHERE g.slug = ($1)::text AND m.status = 'active'   AND (($2)::text = 'open' OR m.weight_class = ($2)::ladder) ORDER BY r.conservative DESC, m.id OFFSET ($4)::int LIMIT ($3)::int) SELECT json_build_object(   'entries', coalesce(json_agg(page ORDER BY page.rank), '[]'::json),   'next_cursor', CASE WHEN count(*) = ($3)::int                       THEN (($4)::int + ($3)::int)::text ELSE NULL END)::text AS body FROM page

description: Query defaults are computed in a map task, not inline in params: db_read folds {"var": ..} nodes only, so an 'or' written directly in params reaches Postgres as a literal object. See orion-gaps.md N1. The body column is cast to text and parsed back by a parse_json task: Orion's db_read goes through sqlx's Any driver, which cannot decode the Postgres json/jsonb type and fails the task outright. Casting keeps response construction in SQL -- see README 'Postgres builds the response JSON' -- at the cost of one extra task.
